newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish pork price rise capped by agency sales.
newsitem.headline: Polish pork price rise capped by agency sales.

text.p: Poland's food market regulator, the Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), said the growth of pork prices on Polish markets has stopped due to its intervention sales of frozen pork, the ARR said on Wednesday.
It said in a statement that it sold 3,900 tonnes of frozen pork at last week's auctions at an average price of 4.50 zlotys per kilogramme, down from 4.52 zlotys/kg the previous week.
"It seems that thanks to intervention sales of pork by the ARR the growth of pork prices was stopped," it said.
The ARR has sold over 30,000 tonnes of pork since the end of July, and has said the intervention sales would continue until the end of the year.

Pork prices have been rising since late June when the Central Statistical Office said that the supply of pork in the third and fouth quarters of this year would be some 150,000 tonnes smaller than in 1995.
Pork prices peaked at over five zlotys/kg in mid-August. --Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
